events.title: Portuguese occupation
hints: A garrison from Goa held the capital island for a decade and a half.
An uprising led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu ended it.
events.summary: In 1558 the Portuguese, based in Goa, seized Malé and garrisoned the capital, seeking to control Indian Ocean trade. After 15 years of rule, a rebellion led by Muhammad Thakurufaanu and his brothers expelled them in 1573, an event still celebrated.

events.title: British protectorate
hints: An atoll sultanate gave up its foreign policy in the late nineteenth century.
The 1887 agreement made it a protected state paying tribute.
events.summary: In 1887 the Sultan accepted British protection under an agreement that left domestic affairs to local rulers while Britain controlled external relations and defence. The Maldives remained a protectorate, linked to Ceylon, until independence in July 1965.

events.title: RAF Gan on Addu Atoll
hints: The southernmost atoll hosted a staging post between the Middle East and the Far East.
A secessionist republic arose among the southern atolls in 1959.
The airbase was handed back in April 1976.
events.summary: Britain turned Gan, in the southernmost atoll, into an RAF staging post in 1957 as other Indian Ocean bases were given up. The British presence, including its labour force, was a source of tension in the southern atolls. Britain handed the airfield to the Maldives on 1 April 1976.
